newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM DRAFTS LAW ON CORPORATE INDEPENDENCE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM DRAFTS LAW ON CORPORATE INDEPENDENCE.

text.p: The Belgian government is working on a draft law for so-called autonomous limited companies, which will have greater independence vis-a-vis shareholders, Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Tuesday.
"We must create a legal instrument which gives Belgian companies the possibility to take the status of an autonomous company," Dehaene told a Belgian parliament committee meeting.

He said the statutes of autonomous companies would be similar to those of Belgian banks, whose statutes already include provisions to avoid conflicts of interest between financial institutions and their shareholders.

Dehaene gave no further details, but referred to planned changes to the statutes of utility holding company Tractebel which are being introduced to counter a perceived threat to Belgian strategic interests in the energy sector from the imminent merger of Tractebel's indirect French parent Compagnie de Suez with Lyonnaise des Eaux .

Last month Tractebel shareholders published a list of proposed changes to the statutes of Tractebel, which all aim at limiting the power of Tractebel's majority shareholder Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) and its French parent Suez.
One of the main proposals was the nomination of independent board members.
